front: La gastronomie française est inscrite au patrimoine immatériel de l'Unesco.
pronunciation: [lah gas-troh-noh-mee frahn-SEZ eh tan-skreet oh pah-tree-mwahn ee-mah-tay-RYEL duh lü-nes-KOH]
back: French gastronomy is listed as UNESCO intangible heritage.
context: More precisely, 'le repas gastronomique des Français' was listed in 2010.

front: Un repas traditionnel comprend une entrée, un plat, du fromage et un dessert.
pronunciation: [an ruh-pah trah-dee-syoh-NEL kohm-prahn tün nahn-TRAY, an PLAH, dü froh-MAHZH ay an deh-SEHR]
back: A traditional meal includes a starter, a main course, cheese and dessert.
context: Cheese comes before dessert in France.

front: Il faut faire revenir les oignons dans le beurre.
pronunciation: [eel foh fehr ruh-vuh-neer lay zoh-NYOHN dahn luh BUHR]
back: Brown the onions in the butter.
context: 'Faire revenir' = to brown, sauté lightly.

front: Laissez mijoter à feu doux pendant deux heures.
pronunciation: [leh-say mee-zhoh-tay ah fuh DOO pahn-dahn duh ZUHR]
back: Let it simmer on low heat for two hours.
context: 'Mijoter' = to simmer. 'À feu doux / vif' = on low / high heat.

front: Le bœuf bourguignon mijote longtemps dans du vin rouge.
pronunciation: [luh buhf boor-ghee-NYOHN mee-zhot lohn-TAHN dahn dü van ROOZH]
back: Beef bourguignon simmers for a long time in red wine.
context: A classic Burgundy dish.

front: Faites dorer le poulet au four.
pronunciation: [fet doh-ray luh poo-LEH oh FOOR]
back: Brown the chicken in the oven.
context: 'Dorer' = to brown, turn golden.

front: Il faut d'abord éplucher et couper les légumes en dés.
pronunciation: [eel foh dah-bor ay-plü-shay ay koo-pay lay lay-güm ahn DAY]
back: First peel and dice the vegetables.
context: 'Éplucher' = to peel. 'En dés' = diced; 'en rondelles' = sliced into rounds.

front: Battez les œufs en neige.
pronunciation: [bah-tay lay zuh ahn NEZH]
back: Beat the egg whites until stiff.
context: 'Battre en neige' = to whisk until stiff peaks form.

front: Préchauffez le four à 180 degrés.
pronunciation: [pray-shoh-fay luh foor ah sahn kah-truh-van duh-GRAY]
back: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
context: Celsius, of course. Older recipes say 'thermostat 6'.

front: Salez et poivrez selon votre goût.
pronunciation: [sah-lay ay pwah-vray suh-lohn voh-truh GOO]
back: Season with salt and pepper to taste.
context: 'Selon votre goût' = to taste.

front: Cette sauce est trop salée.
pronunciation: [set sohs eh troh sah-LAY]
back: This sauce is too salty.
context: Tastes: salé, sucré, amer (bitter), acide, épicé (spicy).

front: La viande est tendre et fondante.
pronunciation: [lah vyahnd eh TAHN-druh ay fohn-DAHNT]
back: The meat is tender and melts in your mouth.
context: 'Fondant' = melting.

front: Ce vin se marie parfaitement avec le fromage.
pronunciation: [suh van suh mah-ree par-fet-mahn ah-vek luh froh-MAHZH]
back: This wine pairs perfectly with the cheese.
context: 'Se marier avec' = to pair well with. 'L'accord mets-vins' = food and wine pairing.

front: Un vin rouge charpenté accompagne bien les viandes rouges.
pronunciation: [an van roozh shar-pahn-TAY ah-kohm-pan-yuh byan lay vyahnd ROOZH]
back: A full-bodied red wine goes well with red meat.
context: 'Charpenté' (well-framed) = full-bodied.

front: Le sommelier nous a conseillé un bordeaux.
pronunciation: [luh soh-muh-lyay noo zah kohn-seh-yay an bor-DOH]
back: The sommelier recommended a Bordeaux.
context: Wines are often named after their region: un bordeaux, un bourgogne, un champagne.

front: Ce vin a un bouquet très fruité.
pronunciation: [suh van ah an boo-keh treh frwee-TAY]
back: This wine has a very fruity bouquet.
context: 'Le bouquet' / 'le nez' = the aroma of a wine.

front: La France compte plus de mille fromages.
pronunciation: [lah frahns kohnt plü duh meel froh-MAHZH]
back: France has more than a thousand cheeses.
context: De Gaulle famously asked how one can govern a country with 246 cheeses.

front: Le camembert est fabriqué en Normandie.
pronunciation: [luh kah-mahn-BEHR eh fah-bree-kay ahn nor-mahn-DEE]
back: Camembert is made in Normandy.
context: Many cheeses have an AOP (protected designation of origin).

front: Le roquefort est un fromage de brebis.
pronunciation: [luh rok-FOR eh tan froh-mahzh duh bruh-BEE]
back: Roquefort is a sheep's milk cheese.
context: Cheeses: de vache (cow), de chèvre (goat), de brebis (sheep).

front: Ce chef a obtenu sa troisième étoile au guide Michelin.
pronunciation: [suh shef ah ob-tuh-nü sah trwah-zyem ay-TWAL oh gheed meesh-LAN]
back: This chef earned his third Michelin star.
context: Three stars = 'worth a special journey'.

front: La cuisine du terroir met en valeur les produits locaux.
pronunciation: [lah kwee-zeen dü teh-RWAHR meh tahn vah-luhr lay proh-dwee loh-KOH]
back: Regional cooking showcases local produce.
context: 'Le terroir' = the land and its character, a key concept in French food and wine.

front: Les produits de saison ont plus de goût.
pronunciation: [lay proh-dwee duh seh-ZOHN ohn plü duh GOO]
back: Seasonal produce has more flavor.
context: 'De saison' = in season.

front: Il faut acheter des produits frais au marché.
pronunciation: [eel foh tahsh-tay day proh-dwee FREH oh mar-SHAY]
back: You should buy fresh produce at the market.
context: 'Les produits frais' = fresh produce.

front: La bouillabaisse est une spécialité marseillaise.
pronunciation: [lah boo-yah-BES eh tün spay-syah-lee-tay mar-seh-YEZ]
back: Bouillabaisse is a Marseille specialty.
context: A fish stew served with 'rouille' sauce and croutons.

front: La choucroute est un plat typique d'Alsace.
pronunciation: [lah shoo-KROOT eh tan plah tee-peek dal-ZAS]
back: Sauerkraut with meats is a typical Alsatian dish.
context: Usually served with sausages and pork.

front: Le cassoulet du Sud-Ouest se compose de haricots blancs et de confit de canard.
pronunciation: [luh kah-soo-LEH dü sü-DWEST suh kohm-pohz duh ah-ree-koh BLAHN ay duh kohn-fee duh kah-NAR]
back: Southwestern cassoulet is made of white beans and duck confit.
context: 'Se composer de' = to be made up of.

front: La tarte Tatin est une tarte aux pommes renversée.
pronunciation: [lah tart tah-TAN eh tün tart oh pum rahn-vehr-SAY]
back: Tarte Tatin is an upside-down apple tart.
context: According to legend, the Tatin sisters invented it by accident.

front: Le chef travaille avec une brigade de vingt cuisiniers.
pronunciation: [luh shef trah-vahy ah-vek ün bree-gad duh van kwee-zee-NYAY]
back: The chef works with a brigade of twenty cooks.
context: 'La brigade de cuisine' = the kitchen team hierarchy.

front: Le service en salle est aussi important que la cuisine.
pronunciation: [luh sehr-vees ahn SAL eh toh-see an-por-tahn kuh lah kwee-ZEEN]
back: Front-of-house service is as important as the cooking.
context: 'En salle' = in the dining room.

front: Les Français passent en moyenne plus de deux heures par jour à table.
pronunciation: [lay frahn-SEH pas ahn mwah-yen plü duh duh zuhr par zhoor ah TAH-bluh]
back: French people spend on average more than two hours a day at the table.
context: 'En moyenne' = on average. France tops OECD rankings on time spent eating.

front: Le goûter est sacré pour les enfants.
pronunciation: [luh goo-TAY eh sah-KRAY poor lay zahn-FAHN]
back: The afternoon snack is sacred for children.
context: 'Le goûter' = the 4 p.m. snack.

front: Ce restaurant propose une cuisine fusion franco-japonaise.
pronunciation: [suh res-toh-rahn proh-pohz ün kwee-zeen fü-ZYOHN frahn-koh-zhah-poh-NEZ]
back: This restaurant serves French-Japanese fusion cuisine.
context: 'Proposer' = to offer (on a menu).

front: La tendance est au fait maison.
pronunciation: [lah tahn-dahns eh toh feh meh-ZOHN]
back: The trend is towards homemade food.
context: Restaurants can display a 'fait maison' logo for dishes made on site.

front: Je suis plutôt sucré que salé.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee plü-toh sü-KRAY kuh sah-LAY]
back: I have more of a sweet tooth than a savory one.
context: 'Être sucré / salé' = to prefer sweet / savory food.

front: Ce plat manque un peu de sel.
pronunciation: [suh plah mahnk an puh duh SEL]
back: This dish needs a little more salt.
context: 'Manquer de' = to lack.

front: Il a eu la main lourde sur le piment.
pronunciation: [ee lah ü lah man LOORD sür luh pee-MAHN]
back: He went overboard with the chili.
context: 'Avoir la main lourde' = to be heavy-handed.

front: Mettez la pâte au frais pendant une heure.
pronunciation: [meh-tay lah paht oh FREH pahn-dahn tün UHR]
back: Put the dough in the fridge for an hour.
context: 'Au frais' = in a cool place, in the fridge. 'La pâte' = dough/batter.

front: Le soufflé est retombé, quelle catastrophe !
pronunciation: [luh soo-flay eh ruh-tohm-BAY, kel kah-tas-TROF]
back: The soufflé has collapsed, what a disaster!
context: 'Retomber' = to fall back down.

front: Ça sent délicieusement bon dans la cuisine.
pronunciation: [sah sahn day-lee-syuhz-mahn BOHN dahn lah kwee-ZEEN]
back: It smells delicious in the kitchen.
context: 'Sentir bon' = to smell good.

front: J'ai l'eau à la bouche !
pronunciation: [zhay loh ah lah BOOSH]
back: My mouth is watering!
context: 'Mettre l'eau à la bouche' = to make your mouth water.

front: On s'est régalés !
pronunciation: [ohn seh ray-gah-LAY]
back: That was a real treat!
context: 'Se régaler' = to enjoy a meal enormously.

front: C'est un vrai cordon-bleu.
pronunciation: [seh tan vreh kor-dohn-BLUH]
back: He's an excellent cook.
context: 'Un cordon-bleu' = a very good home cook.

front: Elle met les petits plats dans les grands pour ses invités.
pronunciation: [el meh lay puh-tee PLAH dahn lay GRAHN poor say zan-vee-TAY]
back: She goes all out for her guests.
context: Idiom: literally 'puts the small dishes in the big ones'.

front: Le pain se pose directement sur la nappe, pas dans l'assiette.
pronunciation: [luh pan suh pohz dee-rek-tuh-mahn sür lah NAP, pah dahn lah-SYET]
back: Bread goes directly on the tablecloth, not on the plate.
context: Table manners: no bread plate in France.

front: À table, on garde les mains sur la table, pas sur les genoux.
pronunciation: [ah TAH-bluh, ohn gard lay man sür lah TAH-bluh, pah sür lay zhuh-NOO]
back: At the table, keep your hands on the table, not on your lap.
context: A French etiquette rule that surprises many visitors.
